fact: An increase in noise should lead to faster decisions, reduced accuracy and, paradoxically, higher confidence.
source_span: An increase in noise should lead to faster decisions , reduced accuracy and , paradoxically , higher confidence . Specifically , were it possible to leave unchanged the expectation of each sample of momentary evidence while boosting the noise associated with it , then the bounded accumulation of the noisier samples should lead to ( i ) lower accuracy when the expectation of the momentary evidence is strong , ( ii ) faster reaction times when the momentary evidence is weak , and ( iii ) increased confidence when the momentary evidence is weak . Increased volatility should affect confidence because it mimics an increase in the diffusion rate . At low coherences in particular , its main effect on the DV is to accelerate its exodus away from neutral ( probability correct = 0 . 5 ) to more extreme values . Therefore , we predicted that volatility would increase confidence at low coherences , for the same reason that it speeds the RT .
abstract_sentence: An increase in noise is predicted to lead to faster decisions, reduced accuracy, and paradoxically higher confidence.

fact: The study introduced a novel sensory manipulation that mimics the addition of unbiased noise to motion-selective regions of visual cortex, which we verified with neuronal recordings from macaque areas MT/MST.
source_span: To test these predictions , we introduce a novel sensory manipulation that mimics the addition of unbiased noise to motion-selective regions of visual cortex , which we verified with neuronal recordings from macaque areas MT/MST . which we verified with neuronal recordings from macaque areas MT/MST . We therefore sought a method to manipulate the variance associated with the neural representation of momentary evidence without affecting its mean. We achieved this with a manipulation of the motion information in a random dot motion (RDM) display, by adding a second level of randomness which increased its volatility but was unbiased with respect to the strength and direction of motion evidence. We verified that the manipulation has the desired properties by recording from direction selective neurons in the middle temporal (MT) and medial superior temporal (MST) areas of the macaque visual cortex. Neurons in these areas are known to represent the momentary evidence in tasks identical to those in our study.

fact: For both humans and monkeys, increasing the noise induced faster decisions and greater confidence over a range of stimuli for which accuracy was minimally impaired.

The main effect of high volatility was to decrease RTs , particularly at the weakest motion strengths ( Figure 3B , bottom row , red ) . The manipulation affected the accuracy only subtly , and this was not statistically reliable for individual subjects in the RT task ( Figure 3B , top row; for the four subjects: p=[0 . 35 , 0 . 65 , 0 . 2 , 0 . 26] , Equation 17 , likelihood-ratio test ) . abstract_sentence: In both humans and monkeys, increasing noise induced faster decisions and greater confidence with minimal impairment of accuracy.

fact: The magnitude of the effects was in agreement with predictions of a bounded evidence accumulation model.
source_span: The magnitude of the effects was in agreement with predictions of a bounded evidence accumulation model . The pattern of results in Figure 3B is consistent with the hypothesis that decisions are made when an accumulation of noisy evidence reaches a bound . Indeed , the smooth curves are fits of this model to the data , where the variance of the momentary evidence is the only parameter that we allowed to change between conditions of high and low volatility . The overall quality of the fits—across all tasks and both species—indicates that the influence of motion strength and volatility on choice, reaction time and confidence can be explained by a common mechanism of bounded evidence accumulation.
abstract_sentence: The magnitude of the effects of noise on decision speed and confidence matched predictions of a bounded evidence accumulation model.

fact: The study applied transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS) to modulate oscillatory activity in a right frontoparietal network supporting working memory.
source_span: Here we applied transcranial alternating current stimulation ( tACS ) to exogenously modulate oscillatory activity in a right frontoparietal network that supports WM . Theta ( 6 Hz ) tACS was applied to the middle frontal gyrus and inferior parietal lobule nodes ( center electrode locations at F4 and P4 ) of the frontoparietal network in synchronous ( 0° relative phase ) and desynchronous ( 180° relative phase ) conditions Ten healthy volunteers performed a session of each tACS condition ( synchronous , desynchronous and sham ) in a pseudo-randomized single-blinded cross-over design .

fact: Mitochondria require mechanisms to eliminate damaged or misfolded proteins to maintain organellar integrity and essential functions.
source_span: Mitochondria require mechanisms to eliminate these proteins to maintain organellar integrity and essential functions ( Voos et al . , 2016 ) . Mitochondria are essential to cellular bioenergetics and metabolism . It is therefore vital that QC mechanisms dispose of damaged proteins that can compromise function .
abstract_sentence: Mitochondria require mechanisms to recognize and remove misfolded proteins to maintain their essential functions.

fact: Quality control pathways for misfolded mitochondrial proteins are poorly defined.
source_span: However , quality control ( QC ) pathways for misfolded mitochondrial proteins remain poorly defined . Thus , a universal MAD pathway for MOM proteins has not been described and many steps in substrate degradation remain unexamined .
abstract_sentence: Quality control pathways for misfolded mitochondrial proteins are not well understood.

fact: Temperature-sensitive peripheral mitochondrial outer membrane proteins sam35-2HAts and sen2-1HAts were established as quality control substrates in Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
source_span: Here , we establish temperature-sensitive ( ts- ) peripheral mitochondrial outer membrane ( MOM ) proteins as novel model QC substrates in Saccharomyces cerevisiae . In this study , we establish temperature-sensitive ( ts- ) peripheral MOM proteins ( sam35-2HAts and sen2-1HAts ) as QC substrates . The ts- nature of these substrates , coupled with their tight association with the MOM , enabled study of their mitochondrial degradation without concerns of mislocalization to the cytosol or elsewhere . Consistent with our microscopy , sam35-2HAts and sen2-1HAts fractionated almost exclusively to the mitochondrial pellet at 37°C ( P; Figure 1D ) .
abstract_sentence: Temperature-sensitive mitochondrial outer membrane proteins were developed as model substrates to study mitochondrial quality control in yeast.

fact: The ts- proteins sen2-1HAts and sam35-2HAts are degraded from the MOM by the ubiquitin-proteasome system.
source_span: The ts- proteins sen2-1HAts and sam35-2HAts are degraded from the MOM by the ubiquitin-proteasome system . While there is no evidence for proteasomes inside mitochondria , the mitochondrial outer membrane ( MOM ) is fully accessible to cytosolic proteasomes . The proteasomal degradation of these MAD QC substrates occurs at the MOM and requires specific cytosolic and mitochondrial UPS components , most of which are conserved in higher eukaryotes . The turnover of sam35-2HAts and sen2-1HAts was assessed at the non-permissive temperature in strains containing conditional mutations in the 20S core ... Both ts- proteins were substantially stabilized in these mutants relative to isogenic WT strains .
abstract_sentence: The temperature-sensitive proteins sam35-2HAts and sen2-1HAts are degraded from the mitochondrial outer membrane by the ubiquitin-proteasome system.

fact: Ubiquitination of sen2-1HAts is mediated by the ubiquitin ligase Ubr1, while sam35-2HAts is ubiquitinated primarily by San1.
source_span: Ubiquitination of sen2-1HAts is mediated by the ubiquitin ligase ( E3 ) Ubr1 , while sam35-2HAts is ubiquitinated primarily by San1 . Interestingly , we found that san1Δ impaired turnover of sam35-2HAts ... while ubr1Δ impaired turnover of sen2-1HAts . While ubr1Δ alone did not affect sam35-2HAts turnover ... loss of Ubr1 in conjunction with san1Δ led to greater stabilization than loss of San1 alone ... Notably , the polyubiquitination of sam35-2HAts and sen2-1HAts was greatly reduced when San1 or Ubr1 , respectively , were deleted .
abstract_sentence: Different ubiquitin ligases mediate ubiquitination of the two mitochondrial outer membrane substrates: Ubr1 for sen2-1HAts and San1 for sam35-2HAts.

fact: Mitochondria-associated degradation (MAD) of both substrates requires the SSA family of Hsp70s and the Hsp40 Sis1, providing the first evidence for chaperone involvement in MAD.
source_span: Mitochondria-associated degradation ( MAD ) of both substrates requires the SSA family of Hsp70s and the Hsp40 Sis1 , providing the first evidence for chaperone involvement in MAD . both sam35-2HAts and sen2-1HAts were strongly stabilized in a conditional yeast strain where three SSA family members are deleted and the fourth (SSA1) is ts- ... the SSA1 chaperone was also required for ubiquitination: despite the accumulation of unmodified sam35-2HAts and sen2-1HAts, ubiquitin-modified forms are dramatically reduced when SSA1 is inactivated ... Depletion of ~90% of Sis1 protein ... slowed the turnover of both sam35-2HAts and sen2-1HAts, while loss of Ydj1 ... did not.
abstract_sentence: Chaperone proteins from the SSA family of Hsp70s and the Hsp40 Sis1 are required for mitochondria-associated degradation of the temperature-sensitive substrates.

fact: The Cdc48-Npl4-Ufd1 AAA-ATPase complex, Doa1 and a mitochondrial pool of the transmembrane Cdc48 adaptor, Ubx2, are implicated in their degradation.
source_span: In addition to a role for the Cdc48-Npl4-Ufd1 AAA-ATPase complex , Doa1 and a mitochondrial pool of the transmembrane Cdc48 adaptor , Ubx2 , are implicated in their degradation . Both sam35-2HAts and sen2-1HAts were stabilized in conditional Cdc48, Npl4, and Ufd1 strains. Accordingly, we detected a relative increase in ubiquitinated sam35-2HAts and sen2-1HAts in Cdc48-Npl4-Ufd1 complex mutants... both substrates remain primarily mitochondrial. Notably, only the loss of Ubx2 significantly stabilized sam35-2HAts and sen2-1HAts.
abstract_sentence: The Cdc48-Npl4-Ufd1 AAA-ATPase complex, Doa1, and the mitochondrial adaptor Ubx2 are involved in the degradation of these mitochondrial outer membrane proteins.

fact: The study reveals a unique quality control pathway for misfolded mitochondrial outer membrane proteins that involves both cytosolic and mitochondrial factors and is distinct from other cellular quality control pathways.
source_span: This study reveals a unique QC pathway comprised of a combination of cytosolic and mitochondrial factors that distinguish it from other cellular QC pathways . Our results reveal a requirement for factors not previously implicated in the degradation of native MAD substrates and the combination of components identified defines a distinct QC pathway . These new mitochondrial model substrates have revealed a tightly-coupled degradation pathway at the MOM that requires both cytosolic and mitochondrial machinery . This MAD QC pathway ... is also not identical to any other cellular QC pathway , although there are points of intersection .
abstract_sentence: This study reveals a unique mitochondrial quality control pathway involving both cytosolic and mitochondrial factors that is distinct from other cellular quality control pathways.

fact: MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are conserved noncoding RNAs that function as posttranscriptional regulators of gene expression; miR-9 is one of the most abundant miRNAs in the developing and adult brain.
source_span: MicroRNAs ( miRNAs ) are conserved noncoding RNAs that function as posttranscriptional regulators of gene expression . Importantly , miR-9 is one of the most abundant miRNAs in the developing and adult brain ( Lagos-Quintana et al . , 2002; Krichevsky et al . , 2003 ) .
abstract_sentence: MicroRNAs are conserved noncoding RNAs that regulate gene expression posttranscriptionally, and miR-9 is one of the most abundant miRNAs in the brain.

fact: The function of miR-9 is well established in neural progenitors, but its role in dendritic and synaptic development in differentiated neurons remains largely unknown.
source_span: Although the function of miR-9 has been well characterized in neural progenitors , its role in dendritic and synaptic development remains largely unknown .
abstract_sentence: The role of miR-9 in dendritic and synaptic development remains largely unknown despite its well-characterized function in neural progenitors.

fact: The study developed a transgenic miRNA sponge mouse line allowing conditional inactivation of the miR-9 family in a spatio-temporal-controlled manner.
source_span: In order to target miR-9 in vivo , we developed a transgenic miRNA sponge mouse line allowing conditional inactivation of the miR-9 family in a spatio-temporal-controlled manner . miRNA sponges are transcripts that carry several in tandem copies of a sequence complementary to the miRNA of interest in their 3′UTRs ( Ebert et al . , 2007 ) . When expressed at high levels , miRNA sponges act as specific competitive inhibitors by binding and sequestering the miRNA of interest . Strategies based on the use of miRNA sponges as dominant negative genetic tools , can overcome the limitations presented by miRNA-gene-KO approaches . Sponges act in trans without interfering with the expression of other genes that could localize with the gene that expresses the miRNA of interest . Moreover , a single sponge transgene allows the simultaneous silencing of ‘seed’ sequence redundant microRNAs encoded at distant loci . Here , we describe for the first time a conditional transgenic sponge mouse model . We derived two different strains for in vivo analysis: ( i ) a reporter mouse line to monitor miR-9 activity with single-cell resolution and ( ii ) a line for miR-9 loss-of-function studies .
abstract_sentence: A transgenic miRNA sponge mouse line was developed to conditionally inactivate the miR-9 family in a spatio-temporal-controlled manner.

fact: Using the miR-9 sponge mouse, the study found that miR-9 controls dendritic growth and synaptic transmission in vivo.
source_span: Using this novel approach , we found that miR-9 controls dendritic growth and synaptic transmission in vivo . Using the latter , we revealed a novel developmental role of miR-9 in the postmitotic differentiation of neurons , as a key regulator of dendritic growth and synaptic transmission in vivo . Pyramidal CA1 neurons from miR-9-SpNestin-Cre mice exhibited a reduction in total dendritic length and arborization complexity compared to control littermates (miR-9-Spfl-Stop). GFP-miR-9 sponge or GFP (control) plus mRFP plasmids were in utero electroporated at E14.5. At P30, pyramidal hippocampal neurons in CA1 were traced... miR-9 sponge-transfected neurons show a reduced total dendritic length and reduced dendritic complexity.
abstract_sentence: miR-9 controls dendritic growth and synaptic transmission in vivo.

fact: miR-9-mediated downregulation of the transcriptional repressor REST is essential for proper dendritic growth.
source_span: Furthermore , we demonstrate that miR-9-mediated downregulation of the transcriptional repressor REST is essential for proper dendritic growth . We found that 13 out of 26 miR-9 predicted targets were upregulated in miR-9-SpNestin-Cre neurons... Interestingly, one of the upregulated mRNAs encodes the global transcriptional repressor element 1 (RE-1) silencing transcription factor (REST/NRSF). Importantly, we also found elevated REST protein levels in sponge expressing neurons. We observed that shREST transfection strongly rescued the dendritic growth defects in miR-9-SpNestin-Cre neurons, indicating that increased REST level is indeed the major mediator of miR-9 effects.
abstract_sentence: miR-9-mediated downregulation of the transcriptional repressor REST is essential for proper dendritic growth.

fact: Thermal biology predicts that vector-borne disease transmission peaks at intermediate temperatures and declines at high and low temperatures.
source_span: Thermal biology predicts that vector-borne disease transmission peaks at intermediate temperatures and declines at high and low temperatures . Both low and high temperatures limit transmission due to low mosquito fecundity and survival at all life stages—thermal responses that are often ignored in transmission models ( Figure 3—figure supplement 2 ) .
abstract_sentence: Vector-borne disease transmission peaks at intermediate temperatures and declines at high and low temperatures.

fact: Thermal optima and limits remain unknown for most vector-borne pathogens.
source_span: However , thermal optima and limits remain unknown for most vector-borne pathogens .
abstract_sentence: Thermal optima and limits remain unknown for most vector-borne pathogens.

fact: We built a mechanistic model for the thermal response of Ross River virus, an important mosquito-borne pathogen in Australia, Pacific Islands, and potentially at risk of emerging worldwide.
source_span: We built a mechanistic model for the thermal response of Ross River virus , an important mosquito-borne pathogen in Australia , Pacific Islands , and potentially at risk of emerging worldwide . Our main model ( ‘full R0 Model , ’ Equation 1 ) assumes temperature drives mosquito density and includes the relevant life history trait thermal responses ( Parham and Michael , 2009; Mordecai et al . , 2013; Mordecai et al . , 2017 ) . We took monthly mean temperatures from WorldClim for seven cities spanning a latitudinal and temperature gradient ( from tropical North to temperate South: Darwin , Cairns , Brisbane , Perth , Sydney , Melbourne , and Hobart ) and calculated the posterior median R0 ( T ) for each month at each location .
abstract_sentence: A mechanistic model was built to describe the thermal response of Ross River virus transmission.

fact: Transmission peaks at moderate temperatures (26.4°C) and declines to zero at thermal limits (17.0 and 31.5°C).
source_span: Transmission peaks at moderate temperatures ( 26 . 4°C ) and declines to zero at thermal limits ( 17 . 0 and 31 . 5°C ) . Transmission potential ( relative R0 from the full R0 model ) peaked at 26 . 4°C , and was positive from 17 . 0–31 . 5°C ( Figure 3 ) . The optimal temperature for transmission is moderate ( 26–27°C; Figure 3 ) , and largely determined by the thermal response of adult mosquito lifespan ( Figure 3—figure supplement 2 ) .
abstract_sentence: Ross River virus transmission peaks at moderate temperatures around 26.4°C and declines to zero outside thermal limits of 17.0°C and 31.5°C.

fact: The model accurately predicts that transmission is year-round endemic in the tropics but seasonal in temperate areas, resulting in the nationwide seasonal peak in human cases.
source_span: The model accurately predicts that transmission is year-round endemic in the tropics but seasonal in temperate areas , resulting in the nationwide seasonal peak in human cases . Temperature suitability for RRV transmission varies seasonally across Australia , based on the full R0 model ... In subtropical and temperate locations ( Brisbane and further south ) , low temperatures force R0 to zero for part of the year ... By contrast , in tropical , northern Australia ( Darwin and Cairns ) , the temperature remains suitable throughout the year ... Temperature explains the geography of year-round endemic versus seasonally epidemic disease ( Figures 5 and 6 ) and accurately predicts the seasonality of human cases at the national scale ( Figure 7 ) .
abstract_sentence: The model accurately predicts that Ross River virus transmission is year-round endemic in the tropics but seasonal in temperate areas, matching the nationwide seasonal peak in human cases.

fact: Climate warming will likely increase transmission in temperate areas (where most Australians live) but decrease transmission in tropical areas where mean temperatures are already near the thermal optimum.
source_span: Climate warming will likely increase transmission in temperate areas ( where most Australians live ) but decrease transmission in tropical areas where mean temperatures are already near the thermal optimum . Climate warming will likely increase the geographic and seasonal range of transmission potential in temperate , southern Australia where most Australians live . However , climate change will likely decrease transmission potential in tropical areas like Darwin , where moderate warming ( ~3°C ) would push temperatures above the upper thermal limit for transmission for most of the year ( Figure 5 ) .
abstract_sentence: Climate warming will likely increase Ross River virus transmission in temperate areas where most Australians live but decrease transmission in tropical areas near the thermal optimum.

fact: A nonlinear mechanistic model is critical for estimating temperature impacts on transmission because the effect of increasing temperature by a few degrees can have a positive, negligible, or negative impact on R0 along different parts of the thermal response curve.
source_span: A nonlinear mechanistic model is critical for estimating temperature impacts on transmission because the effect of increasing temperature by a few degrees can have a positive , negligible , or negative impact on R0 along different parts of the thermal response curve . Nonlinear thermal responses are particularly important for predicting how transmission will change under future climate regimes .
abstract_sentence: Nonlinear mechanistic models are critical for predicting temperature impacts on Ross River virus transmission because temperature changes can have positive, negligible, or negative effects depending on the thermal response curve.

fact: Motor cortical beta oscillations have been reported for decades, but their behavioral correlates remain unresolved.
source_span: Motor cortical beta oscillations have been reported for decades , yet their behavioral correlates remain unresolved .
abstract_sentence: Motor cortical beta oscillations have been reported for decades, but their behavioral correlates remain unresolved.

fact: Three macaque monkeys were trained to perform both a standard arm-reaching task and a novel sequential beta neurofeedback arm-reaching task while neural activity was recorded.
source_span: To explore how beta oscillations reflect changes in spiking activity and movement parameters , we trained three macaque monkeys to perform a typical center-out arm-reaching task ( CO task , Figure 1a ) , and a novel sequential beta neurofeedback arm-reaching task ( NR task , Figure 1b ) . Three male rhesus macaques ( Macaca mulatta ) were chronically implanted with arrays of 128 Teflon-coated tungsten microwire electrodes ... in the left upper arm area of primary motor cortex ( M1 ) and posterior dorsal premotor cortex ( PMd ).
abstract_sentence: We recorded multi-scale neural activity from motor cortex while three macaques performed a novel neurofeedback task to study links between neural activity, beta oscillations, and behavior.

fact: The study used a novel neurofeedback task in which three macaque monkeys volitionally modulated their motor cortical beta oscillatory power before executing an arm reach.
source_span: Subjects volitionally brought their beta oscillatory power to an instructed state and subsequently executed an arm reach . Subjects modulated endogenous motor cortical local field potential signals to move the vertical position of the beta cursor ... When the beta cursor fell in the beta target , subjects were required to hold within the beta target for 450 ms ... Subjects then executed a right-arm reach from the central target to a peripheral target to receive a liquid reward . The neurofeedback epoch accomplished the goal of bringing beta power to different levels ... At the time of the go cue there is a significant group difference in normalized beta power for the four different neurofeedback target conditions These three metrics ... demonstrate that the neurofeedback epoch served to increase and decrease beta oscillatory power prior to the arm-reaching epoch
abstract_sentence: Monkeys volitionally modulated their motor cortical beta oscillatory power before executing an arm reach in a novel neurofeedback task.

fact: Reaches preceded by a reduction in beta power exhibited significantly faster movement onset times than reaches preceded by an increase in beta power.
source_span: Reaches preceded by a reduction in beta power exhibited significantly faster movement onset times than reaches preceded by an increase in beta power . In all three animals, trials with high beta power targets had subsequent reaches with slower movement onset times (Figure 3a–c, two-tailed Cuzick’s test, Monkey S: z = 5.763, p=8.267e-09, n = 1183, Monkey C: z = 11.987, p<5e-20, n = 2168, Monkey G: z = 5.856, p=4.729e-09, n = 1028). Despite the different approaches that were taken to increase and decrease beta power across animals there is still a consistent effect of high versus low beta power on movement onset times , increasing confidence that the oscillation is a reliable marker of the observed behavior .
abstract_sentence: Reaches preceded by a reduction in beta power exhibited significantly faster movement onset times than reaches preceded by an increase in beta power.

fact: Population neural activity shifted farther from a movement onset state during beta oscillations that were neurofeedback-induced or naturally occurring during reaching tasks.
source_span: Further , population neural activity was found to shift farther from a movement onset state during beta oscillations that were neurofeedback-induced or naturally occurring during reaching tasks . Here , we report both changes in motor behavior following performance of neurofeedback during a sequential neurofeedback-reaching task , and a neural population shift that mirrors the observed change in motor behavior . Notably , this shift in neural population was also seen in naturally occurring beta oscillations during reaching tasks , suggesting that beta oscillations reflect a common signature of spiking patterns even in different task contexts .
abstract_sentence: Population neural activity shifted farther from a movement onset state during beta oscillations that were neurofeedback-induced or naturally occurring during reaching tasks.

fact: This study establishes a population neural basis for slowed movement onset following periods of beta oscillatory activity.
source_span: This finding establishes a population neural basis for slowed movement onset following periods of beta oscillatory activity . Our result that volitionally increasing and decreasing motor cortical beta power with neurofeedback precedes slower and faster movement onset times supports the hypothesis that beta oscillations are linked to neural patterns that slow onset of new movements ( Gilbertson et al . , 2005 ). The hypothesis that encoding of specific movements is compromised with beta oscillations is further supported by experiments showing that in a delayed reaching task similar to the CO task here , movement cues associated with more uncertainty are correlated with higher beta power during preparatory periods than movement cues associated with certainty ( Tzagarakis et al . , 2010 ) . Further , during spike-driven cursor brain-machine interface tasks in which subjects are not moving , periods of beta oscillatory activity correspond to inferior neural decoding ( Milekovic et al . , 2013 ) and slower cursor movements ( Ranade et al . , 2009 ) , suggesting that the population contains less specific directional information that can be used to move the prosthetic cursor .
abstract_sentence: This finding establishes a population neural basis for slowed movement onset following periods of beta oscillatory activity.

fact: Marburg virus, Kaposi's sarcoma-associated herpesvirus (KSHV), and Dengue virus activate and benefit from expression of the transcription regulator nuclear erythroid 2-related factor 2 (Nrf2), whereas Nrf2 activation counters HIV infection in macrophages.
source_span: Marburg virus , the Kaposi's sarcoma-associated herpesvirus ( KSHV ) and Dengue virus all activate , and benefit from , expression of the transcription regulator nuclear erythroid 2-related factor 2 ( Nrf2 ) . Finally , the discovery that Nrf2 mobilization counters HIV infection in macrophages stands in contrast with recent work showing that Marburg and Dengue virus as well as KSHV initiate and benefit from increased Nrf2 expression [30 , 32 , 34 , 41] .
abstract_sentence: Some viruses activate and benefit from Nrf2 expression, but HIV is different.

fact: The impact of Nrf2 activation on human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection had not been tested prior to this study.
source_span: The impact of Nrf2 activation on human immunodeficiency virus ( HIV ) infection has not been tested .
abstract_sentence: The effect of Nrf2 activation on HIV infection had not been studied before.

fact: Sulforaphane (SFN), a compound produced in cruciferous vegetables after mechanical damage, mobilizes Nrf2 to potently reprogram cellular gene expression.
source_span: Sulforaphane ( SFN ) , produced in cruciferous vegetables after mechanical damage , mobilizes Nrf2 to potently reprogram cellular gene expression . SFN is a powerful mobilizer of the transcription factor nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 ( Nrf2 ) [22–24] . Nrf2 , a master regulator of the antioxidant response [25 , 26] , ...
abstract_sentence: Sulforaphane (SFN) activates Nrf2 by mobilizing it to change gene expression.

fact: SFN blocks HIV infection in primary macrophages but not in primary T cells.
source_span: Here we show for the first time that SFN blocks HIV infection in primary macrophages but not in primary T cells . Thus, SFN acts to block single-round HIV-1 infections in primary hMDMs but not in primary T cells. Further investigation will be required to determine why SFN fails to block infection in T cells , whether the same pathway could be exploited there as well or whether the restriction can be activated directly by other means .
abstract_sentence: SFN blocks HIV infection in primary macrophages but not in primary T cells.

fact: SFN blocks HIV infection in PMA-differentiated promonocytic cell lines but not in other tested cell lines; siRNA depletion of Nrf2 increases HIV infectivity and reduces SFN's antiviral effect in primary macrophages.
source_span: Similarly SFN blocks infection in PMA-differentiated promonocytic cell lines , but not in other cell lines tested . siRNA-mediated depletion of Nrf2 boosted HIV infectivity in primary macrophages and reduced the anti-viral effects of SFN treatment . We detected no inhibition of HIV infection after SFN treatment in HeLa, HEK293T or GHOST cells but SFN markedly decreased evidence of infection in U937 and THP1 cultures. In the absence of SFN , depletion of Nrf2 caused a significant increase in luciferase activity indicating that Nrf2 is detrimental to HIV infection in macrophages and that the basal level of Nrf2 that is present in macrophages is sufficient for establishing some anti-viral activity ( Fig 6D ) .
abstract_sentence: SFN blocks HIV infection in macrophage-like cell lines and this antiviral effect depends on Nrf2.

fact: SFN treatment blocks HIV infection after entry but before formation of 2-LTR circles, similar to SAMHD1 and MX2, but does not upregulate these antiviral proteins.
source_span: We further found that , like the type I interferon-induced cellular anti-viral proteins SAMHD1 and MX2 , SFN treatment blocks infection after entry , but before formation of 2-LTR circles . This limits the Nrf2-mediated block to steps that extend from attachment of the virus to the cell through transcription from the provirus . ... The vehicle- and SFN-treated samples showed similar levels of late reverse transcription product , indicating that SFN , unlike AZT , did not hinder replication steps from viral entry through reverse transcription ( Fig 7A ) . When we tested for 2-LTR circles ... we found that these were clearly decreased in the AZT and SFN samples relative to the vehicle controls ( Fig 7B ) . Alu-PCR , testing for integrated proviral sequences , also showed that these were similarly decreased in AZT- and SFN-treated cultures ... We found that SFN counters infection whether viral entry is mediated through HIV Env or VSV-G glycoproteins ( Figs 1B versus 5E ) . This suggests a post-entry block as these glycoproteins engage different entry mechanisms . Interestingly however , neither SAMHD1 nor MX2 were upregulated .
abstract_sentence: SFN blocks HIV infection after viral entry but before integration, similar to known antiviral proteins, without upregulating those proteins.

fact: SFN acts through the transcription factor Nrf2 to execute most of its known functions, including blocking HIV infection in macrophages.
source_span: SFN acts through Nrf2 to execute the majority of its known functions [44–46] . DMF and MMF , like SFN , increase levels of Nrf2 [55] , suggesting that these compounds also block HIV in macrophages through Nrf2 .
abstract_sentence: SFN's antiviral activity is mediated through Nrf2 activation.

fact: Nrf2 activation can potently block HIV infection and highlights a novel way to trigger this inhibition, contrasting with other viruses that benefit from Nrf2.
source_span: This shows for the first time that Nrf2 action can potently block HIV infection and highlights a novel way to trigger this inhibition . Together this work shows that , in contrast to Marburg , Dengue and KSHV , HIV is blocked through Nrf2 and sets the stage for discovering the mechanism underlying this restriction .
abstract_sentence: Nrf2 activation can potently block HIV infection, revealing a new antiviral mechanism.

fact: Aedes-borne arboviruses such as dengue and Zika continue to cause epidemics worldwide.
source_span: Aedes-borne arboviruses continue to precipitate epidemics worldwide .
abstract_sentence: Aedes-borne arboviruses such as dengue and Zika continue to cause epidemics worldwide.

fact: The Dominican Republic experienced a large dengue epidemic followed closely by Zika virus cases, providing an opportunity to study differences in transmission between these two flaviviruses.
source_span: In Dominican Republic , the appearance of Zika virus cases that closely followed a large dengue epidemic provided an opportunity to study the different transmission drivers behind these two flaviviruses . In 2015/early-2016 , a major dengue outbreak affected the island ... As this outbreak abated , the first cases of Zika were detected .
abstract_sentence: The Dominican Republic experienced a large dengue epidemic followed closely by Zika virus cases, providing an opportunity to study differences in transmission between these two flaviviruses.

fact: Retrospective surveillance data from the Dominican Republic were used to analyze national-scale outbreaks of dengue, Zika, and associated Guillain-Barre syndrome cases.

abstract_sentence: Retrospective surveillance data from the Dominican Republic were used to analyze national-scale outbreaks of dengue, Zika, and associated Guillain-Barre syndrome cases.

fact: Dengue cases were predominantly reported in individuals under 20 years old, while Zika infections were more evenly distributed across age groups.
source_span: Expectedly , box plots showed that 75% of dengue was reported in those aged <20 years while Zika infections were more widely dispersed among the population . 75% of all dengue cases occurred before the age of 20 compared with ~42 for Zika.
abstract_sentence: Dengue cases were predominantly reported in individuals under 20 years old, while Zika infections were more evenly distributed across age groups.

source_span: Dengue attack rates were marginally higher among males at 25 . 9 per 10 , 000 population vs . 21 . 5 per 10 , 000 population for females . Dengue infections were more common among men (54.5%) than women (45.5%) in the Dominican Republic. Age-adjusted attack rates of dengue were higher in males (25.9 per 10,000) than females (21.5 per 10,000) in the Dominican Republic.
abstract_sentence: Dengue attack rates were slightly higher in males compared to females in the Dominican Republic.

fact: Zika infections were significantly more common among females, with about 74% of cases occurring in women.
source_span: Zika infections appeared to be highly clustered among females ( 73 . 8% ( 95% CI 72 . 6% , 75 . 0%; p<0 . 05 ) ) ; age-adjusted Zika attack rates among females were 7 . 64 per 10 , 000 population compared with 2 . 72 per 10 , 000 population among males . Zika infections were more common among women (73.8%) than men (26.2%) in the Dominican Republic.
abstract_sentence: Zika infections were significantly more common among females, with about 74% of cases occurring in women.

fact: The basic reproduction number (R0) for Zika was higher in females than in males in the Dominican Republic.
source_span: R0 calculations stratified by sex also showed a significantly higher metric among females: 1 . 84 ( 1 . 82 , 1 . 87; p<0 . 05 ) when compared to males at 1 . 72 ( 1 . 69 , 1 . 75; p<0 . 05 ) . Stratifying by sex, the national R0 for males was 1.72 ... and 1.84 ... for females.
abstract_sentence: The basic reproduction number (R0) for Zika was higher in females than in males in the Dominican Republic.

fact: Guillain-Barre syndrome (GBS) attack rates were slightly higher in males than females during the Zika outbreak.
source_span: GBS attack rates stratified by sex revealed slightly higher risk in males vs . females , at 0 . 62 and 0 . 57 per 10 , 000 population respectively .
abstract_sentence: Guillain-Barre syndrome (GBS) attack rates were slightly higher in males than females during the Zika outbreak.

fact: Existing dengue immunity appears to have little impact on the population-level attack rates of Zika virus.

abstract_sentence: Existing dengue immunity appears to have little impact on the population-level attack rates of Zika virus.

fact: Community awareness campaigns likely influenced increased reporting of Zika infections among women of reproductive age.
source_span: The findings indicate that community awareness campaigns , through influencing short-term health seeking behaviour , remain the most plausible mechanism behind increased reporting among women of reproductive age , although biological susceptibility cannot yet be ruled out . Evidence also suggests a greater burden of Zika among women, however this is most likely due to increased health-seeking behaviour rather than biological mechanisms, yet the latter still cannot be ruled out. If correct, targeted advocacy campaigns are effective at changing short-term behaviour and are recommended during Zika epidemics.
abstract_sentence: Community awareness campaigns likely influenced increased reporting of Zika infections among women of reproductive age.

fact: Media campaigns and screening are recommended for women of reproductive age during Zika outbreaks.
source_span: Media campaigns and screening are therefore recommended for women of reproductive age during Zika outbreaks .
abstract_sentence: Media campaigns and screening are recommended for women of reproductive age during Zika outbreaks to improve detection and response.

abstract_sentence: Future research should investigate clinical outcomes of Zika infection among individuals previously exposed to dengue virus.

fact: Under nitrogen deprivation, filaments of the cyanobacterium Anabaena develop a one-dimensional pattern of nitrogen-fixing heterocysts separated by about ten photosynthetic vegetative cells.
source_span: Under nitrogen deprivation , filaments of the cyanobacterium Anabaena undergo a process of development , resulting in a one-dimensional pattern of nitrogen-fixing heterocysts separated by about ten photosynthetic vegetative cells .
abstract_sentence: Under nitrogen deprivation, Anabaena filaments develop a one-dimensional pattern of nitrogen-fixing heterocysts separated by about ten photosynthetic vegetative cells.

fact: The transcription factor HetR is essential for heterocyst differentiation in Anabaena, and its expression was studied using a chromosomal hetR-gfp fusion.
source_span: We studied the statistics of fluctuations of gene expression of HetR , a transcription factor essential for heterocyst differentiation , both under steady-state growth in nitrogen-rich conditions and at different times following nitrogen deprivation , using a chromosomally-encoded translational hetR-gfp fusion . Our study was conducted using a chromosomal hetR-gfp fusion , thereby avoiding any contribution to fluctuations stemming from cell-cell variability in plasmid copy number , which would preclude accurate evaluation of both noise and cell-cell correlations in expression . As a reporter , a fusion to a fragment of the N-terminal part of the protein was constructed rather than a traditional transcriptional fusion because with the N-terminal translational fusion , expression of the gene with all its transcription and translation start signals is tested .
abstract_sentence: HetR is a transcription factor essential for heterocyst differentiation, studied using a chromosomal hetR-gfp fusion under nitrogen-rich and nitrogen-deprived conditions.

fact: Gene expression fluctuations of hetR in nearby cells along Anabaena filaments are coupled with a spatial range of about two to three cells.
source_span: Statistical analysis of fluorescence at the individual cell level in wild-type and mutant filaments demonstrates that expression fluctuations of hetR in nearby cells are coupled , with a characteristic spatial range of circa two to three cells , setting the scale for cellular interactions along a filament . In contrast to unicellular organisms in which fluctuations in gene expression between different cells are independent , we expected to find correlations between the fluctuations in hetR-gfp expression in Anabaena along filaments . Irrespective of the strain , the behavior indicates that gene expression between cells under nitrogen-rich conditions is correlated up to distances of two to three cells . The spatial autocorrelation function of hetR-gfp expression along filaments shows that correlations between neighboring cells die out after two to three cells , a range of correlations that is shorter than the characteristic scale of developmental patterns .
abstract_sentence: Expression fluctuations of hetR in nearby cells along Anabaena filaments are coupled with a spatial range of about two to three cells.

fact: Intercellular molecular transfer contributes more to correlations in hetR expression between cells than cell division.
source_span: Correlations between cells predominantly arise from intercellular molecular transfer and less from cell division . The dominant part of the observed correlations must derive from intercellular molecular transfer: had the measured correlations been due exclusively to cell division , there would be no difference between the autocorrelation functions pertaining to the different mutant strains . Together , these analyses support the notion that PatS or a derivative thereof is transferred between neighboring cells , consistently with results obtained with filaments that have already sensed nitrogen deprivation .
abstract_sentence: Correlations in hetR expression between cells mainly arise from intercellular molecular transfer rather than cell division.

fact: Cell-to-cell fluctuations of HetR include essential contributions from the developmental network even when not induced, with clusters of cells expressing hetR-gfp existing under nitrogen-rich conditions and fluctuations building up after nitrogen step-down.
source_span: We conclude that cell-to-cell fluctuations of the master regulator HetR in Anabaena are complex and include essential contributions from the developmental network even when the latter is not induced . Our observations show that these clusters already exist under nitrogen-rich conditions , whereas previous investigations had shown that the differentiation process initiates in small clusters of cells that are later resolved into single heterocysts , after the environmental cue is given . Our measurements of the statistical properties of fluctuations in gene expression of hetR-gfp well after the developmental network has sensed nitrogen step-down , but possibly before a final commitment has been established show that the primordial fluctuations under nitrogen-rich conditions and those at early times after nitrogen step-down , e . g . 3 hours , are statistically similar . Our results show that fluctuations can build up from an underlying pattern of expression under nitrogen-replete conditions in which important regulators are already expressed, and evolve to intermediate states in which fluctuations are positively correlated in clusters of cells. These latter resolve after commitment into single heterocysts using lateral inhibition, supporting a two-stage model of development.
abstract_sentence: Fluctuations in hetR expression under nitrogen-rich conditions form clusters of cells and build up into patterns after nitrogen deprivation, indicating continuity in expression dynamics.

fact: Basal expression of the HetR inhibitor PatS, cell-cell communication influenced by septal protein SepJ, and positive HetR auto-regulation are essential determinants of fluctuations in hetR expression under nitrogen-rich conditions.
source_span: We found that under nitrogen-rich conditions , basal , steady-state expression of the HetR inhibitor PatS , cell-cell communication influenced by the septal protein SepJ and positive HetR auto-regulation are essential determinants of fluctuations in hetR expression and its distribution along filaments . The histograms of the ΔpatS and ΔsepJ mutants are significantly broader than the WT histogram , and their respective means ±std ( 18±8 and 19±7 ) larger than the WT’s ( 13±4 ) . The histogram of ΔpatS exhibits a particularly long tail of high fluorescence values , which is consistent with a possible lack of inhibition of hetR expression . The noise of hetR-gfp in the ΔpatS background is by far the largest among all strains ... The level of noise characterizing ΔsepJ filaments lies intermediate between those of the WT and the ΔpatS strains . In contrast , the strain lacking HetR exhibits the smallest level of noise . The cigar shape of the scatter for ΔpatS ( Pearson coefficient = 0 . 40 ) reveals a larger statistical tendency for nearest neighbors cells to have similar fluorescence than in the WT ( Pearson coefficient = 0 . 25 ) . In contrast , the observed tendency of some highly fluorescent cells to have weakly fluorescent neighbors in ΔsepJ filaments ( Pearson coefficient = 0 . 05 ) , suggests that expression fluctuations in this strain are less constrained than in the WT .
abstract_sentence: Under nitrogen-rich conditions, basal expression of PatS, cell-cell communication via SepJ, and positive HetR auto-regulation determine hetR expression fluctuations and distribution along filaments.

fact: PatS and HetN differ as HetR inhibitors under nitrogen-poor conditions, and septal proteins SepJ and FraC/FraD differ in their specificity influencing hetR expression.
source_span: A comparison between the expression of hetR-gfp under nitrogen-rich and nitrogen-poor conditions highlights the differences between the two HetR inhibitors PatS and HetN , as well as the differences in specificity between the septal proteins SepJ and FraC/FraD . The hetR-gfp fusion was transferred to wild-type Anabaena ( WT ) and mutant strains with deletions in the patS regulatory gene , in the hetN regulatory gene , in the sepJ gene encoding septal protein SepJ , and in the fraC and fraD genes encoding septal proteins FraC and FraD ... We investigated two mutant strains , ΔsepJ and ΔfraC/ΔfraD , both of which lack proteins that are thought to contribute to intercellular septal junction complexes and cell-cell communication . These data suggest that FraC/FraD proteins are involved in the late time transport of specific metabolic and/or regulatory factors that may be different from those transported by SepJ , negatively impacting hetR expression in neighboring cells .
abstract_sentence: The HetR inhibitors PatS and HetN differ in their roles and timing during heterocyst pattern formation, and septal proteins SepJ and FraC/FraD differ in specificity affecting hetR expression.

fact: Proteins involved in activation, inhibition, and cell-cell communication combine with stochastic gene expression to control coupled fluctuations that give rise to the one-dimensional developmental pattern in Anabaena.
source_span: Our results show that proteins involved in these basic ingredients combine together in the presence of inevitable stochasticity in gene expression , to control the coupled fluctuations of gene expression that give rise to a one-dimensional developmental pattern in this organism . We found that key factors known to act during differentiation following nitrogen deprivation can also play a role before differentiation has been triggered , setting an underlying pattern of spatial correlations of gene expression along filaments , on which the developmental pattern may later be built . In an organism with no specific limit to the number of its cells and on which morphogen gradient fields are not imposed from the outside such as in Drosophila , a developmental pattern can arise from fluctuations in gene expression and activation-inhibition mechanisms such as originally envisioned by Turing . Therefore, expression fluctuations are key determinants in the decision of cells whether to differentiate or not, together with other factors such as cell division and biased inheritance of specific factors, as well as the marked tendency for heterocysts to form at the ends of finite filaments, thereby imposing a strong constraint on the phase of the patterns that form.
abstract_sentence: Proteins involved in activation, inhibition, and cell-cell communication combine with stochastic gene expression to control coupled fluctuations that generate the one-dimensional developmental pattern in Anabaena filaments.

source_span: We developed and field-tested an innovative integrated NTD mapping protocol ( Integrated Threshold Mapping ( ITM ) Methodology ) for lymphatic filariasis ( LF ) , trachoma , schistosomiasis and soil-transmitted helminths ( STH ) .

fact: The ITM protocol is designed to be resource-efficient, and its specific purpose is to determine whether a threshold to trigger public health interventions in an implementation unit has been attained.
source_span: The protocol is designed to be resource-efficient , and its specific purpose is to determine whether a threshold to trigger public health interventions in an implementation unit has been attained . We describe an integrated NTD mapping methodology ( Integrated Threshold Mapping ) that can be used as an operational tool by Ministries of Health in NTD-endemic countries to determine if the threshold needed to launch disease-specific public health intervenions has been reached .
abstract_sentence: The ITM protocol is resource-efficient and determines if disease thresholds for public health interventions have been reached.

fact: The protocol relies on World Health Organization (WHO) recommended indicators in the disease-specific age groups, using the district as the sampling frame except for schistosomiasis where the sub-district is used.
source_span: The protocol relies on World Health Organization ( WHO ) recommended indicators in the disease-specific age groups . For each disease , the sampling frame was the district , but for schistosomiasis , the sub-district rather than the ecological zone was used . With the exception of some minor modifications for trachoma , we have retained the key indicators and age groups used in the disease-specific WHO mapping guidelines , but have adapted the sampling methodologies . The ITM protocol maintains the WHO-recommended disease indicators and thresholds for LF , schistosomiasis and STH , but we used a novel sampling frame for more practical field implementation .
abstract_sentence: The ITM protocol uses WHO-recommended disease indicators and age groups, adapting sampling frames for practical field use.

The integrated approach proved to be more efficient in cost , transport , time in the field and the use of human resources . The ITM methodology used one vehicle to transport the team , versus 3 used in the WHO methodologies , employed a 5-member team instead of a 7-member team , and took about half as much time to implement as the WHO methodologies .

fact: Notch signaling is increased with age in Drosophila female germline stem cells (GSCs), resulting in their removal from the niche.
source_span: Here , we report that Notch signaling is increased with age in Drosophila female germline stem cells ( GSCs ) , and this results in their removal from the niche . However , we observed a 20% increase of E ( spl ) m7-lacZ expression in aged GSCs ( n = 54 , P<0 . 05 ) as compared to their younger counterparts . However , we observed that bam mutant GSCs which escaped from the niche still exhibited increased Notch signaling as they aged , suggesting that direct contact between GSCs and the niche is not required for such signaling . Expression of Sxl in the anterior-most germ cells (including GSCs) of germaria decreased with age... Our results suggest that the induction of Notch signaling with age in GSCs is at least partly mediated by Sxl.
abstract_sentence: Notch signaling is increased with age in Drosophila female germline stem cells (GSCs), resulting in their removal from the niche.

fact: GSCs with low Notch signaling have increased adhesion to the niche via E-cadherin, allowing them to out-compete neighbors with higher Notch.
source_span: Clonal analysis revealed that GSCs with low levels of Notch signaling exhibit increased adhesiveness to the niche , thereby out-competing their neighbors with higher levels of Notch; adhesiveness is altered through regulation of E-cadherin expression . E-cadherin is a cell-cell adhesion molecule required for GSC-niche adhesion [12]; we found that its expression was significantly increased in mutant GSC-niche junctions of N55e11 germaria as compared to neighboring normal GSC-niche junctions at one week ( 98±5 vs . 82±5 arbitrary units , P<0 . 05 ) and two weeks ( 91±7 vs . 71±6 arbitrary units , P<0 . 05 ) ACI ( Fig . 3A–B ) . These results suggest that low levels of Notch signaling in GSCs increases GSC adhesion to the niche , thereby allowing the cells to out-compete their normal wild-type GSCs . Conversely , the proportion of N55e11 mutant GSCs expressing shgRNAi remained at a similar level to controls ( Fig . 4E ) , indicating that Notch signaling controls GSC competitiveness in an E-cadherin-dependent manner .
abstract_sentence: GSCs with low levels of Notch signaling exhibit increased adhesiveness to the niche, out-competing neighbors with higher Notch levels through regulation of E-cadherin expression.

fact: Increasing Notch signaling in GSCs speeds up their loss from the niche, partly through the action of the Sex lethal protein.
source_span: Experimental enhancement of Notch signaling in GSCs hastens their age-dependent loss from the niche , and such loss is at least partially mediated by Sex lethal . We therefore investigated whether Sxl also controls Notch signaling in GSCs ( Fig . 6 ) . We first generated mosaic germaria carrying GSCs with two copies of sxlf2 ( identified by the absence of GFP ) , a hypomorphic allele [37] . These sxlf2 mutant GSCs exhibited increased Notch signaling ( as determined by examining the expression of E ( spl ) m7-lacZ ) as compared to their neighboring control GSCs ( Fig . 6A–C ) . Consistent with our finding that elevating Notch signaling in GSCs induces their loss from the niche , sxlfs3 ( anothour hypomorphic allele [38] ) mutant GSCs were rapidly lost by two weeks ACI ( S1 Table ) . These results indicate that Sxl suppresses Notch signaling in GSCs.
abstract_sentence: Experimental enhancement of Notch signaling in GSCs accelerates their age-dependent loss from the niche, partially mediated by Sex lethal.

fact: Blocking Notch signaling in GSCs does not prevent their age-related loss and does not change BMP signaling that supports their renewal.
source_span: However , disruption of Notch signaling in GSCs does not delay GSC loss during aging , and nor does it affect BMP signaling , which promotes self-renewal of GSCs . Division was unaffected in GSCs homozygous for N55ell , a null allele [23] ( Fig . 1D ) ; these mutant GSCs exhibited decreased levels of Notch signaling as compared to their neighboring control GSCs ( S4 Fig . ) . However , the levels of two well-established reporters of BMP signaling [30] , phosphorylated ( p ) Mad ( pMad ) and Dad-lacZ , were unaffected in Notch signaling-defective GSCs , as compared to their neighboring control GSCs . Although inhibition of Notch expression increased E-cadherin expression at the GSC-niche junction, this was not sufficient to suppress age-dependent GSC loss.
abstract_sentence: Disruption of Notch signaling in GSCs does not delay GSC loss during aging and does not affect BMP signaling, which promotes GSC self-renewal.

fact: Notch signaling decreases with age in niche cells, which maintain niche integrity and help retain GSCs.
source_span: Finally , we show that in contrast to GSCs , Notch activation in the niche ( which maintains niche integrity , and thus mediates GSC retention ) is reduced with age , indicating that Notch signaling regulates GSC niche occupancy both intrinsically and extrinsically . We observed that Notch signaling in the niche and GSCs was affected by age in different ways; during aging , Notch signaling was decreased in the niche , but increased in GSCs .
abstract_sentence: Notch activation in the niche cells, which maintains niche integrity and mediates GSC retention, is reduced with age.

fact: Notch signaling controls stem cell adhesion to the niche during aging and is similarly involved in cancer cell adhesion.
source_span: Our findings expose a novel role of Notch signaling in controlling GSC-niche adhesion in response to aging , and are also of relevance to metastatic cancer cells , in which Notch signaling suppresses cell adhesion .
abstract_sentence: Notch signaling regulates GSC-niche adhesion in response to aging, a novel role relevant also to metastatic cancer cells where Notch suppresses cell adhesion.

fact: Proteochemometric models combining chemical and protein target properties in a single bioactivity model were applied to improve HIV drug resistance prediction.
source_span: To explore the added value of chemical similarity inclusion we applied proteochemometric models, combining chemical and protein target properties in a single bioactivity model. Hence it is likely that also for established drugs, chemical similarity can improve models by explicitly taking the concept of drug – target interaction into account, which is then combined with mutational information of the drug target itself. This technique is called proteochemometric (PCM) modeling.
abstract_sentence: Proteochemometric models combining chemical and protein target properties in a single bioactivity model were applied to improve HIV drug resistance prediction.

fact: The study used a large clinical database containing approximately 300,000 drug-mutant bioactivity data points across multiple drug classes and thousands of HIV mutants.
source_span: Our dataset was a large scale clinical database of genotypic and phenotypic information (in total ca. 300,000 drug-mutant bioactivity data points, 4 (NNRTI), 8 (NRTI) or 9 (PI) drugs, and 10,700 (NNRTI) 10,500 (NRTI) or 27,000 (PI) mutants). fact: Proteochemometric models achieved a prediction error below 0.5 Log Fold Change and outperformed sequence-only models in resistance classification and Log Fold Change prediction.
source_span: Our models achieved a prediction error below 0.5 Log Fold Change. Moreover, when directly compared with previously published sequence data derived models PCM performed better in resistance classification and prediction of Log Fold Change (0.76 log units versus 0.91). Indeed, we found that also here PCM outperforms sequence only models in all drug classes. In all cases the prediction error improves by approximately 11% (with a similar improvement of correlation coefficient). Our PCM models clearly outperform sequence only models . For each class the PCM models predict the Log FC more accurately . This is indicated by the smaller RMSE ( 0 . 53 log units versus 0 . 68 log units for the NRTIs; 0 . 65 log units versus 0 . 75 log units for the PIs , and 0 . 85 log units versus 1 . 3 log units for the NNRTIs ) and also by a higher CCP ( 68% versus 54% for the NRTIs , 78% versus 75% for the PIs , and 89% versus 78% for the NNRTIs ) . Both in internal validation and validation on unseen data our model showed performance comparable to assay reliability and better than sequence only models;
abstract_sentence: Proteochemometric models achieved a prediction error below 0.5 Log Fold Change and outperformed sequence-only models in resistance classification and Log Fold Change prediction.

fact: The models confirmed known and identified previously unpublished resistance-conferring mutations in HIV Reverse Transcriptase and HIV Protease.
source_span: Furthermore, we were able to successfully confirm both known and identify previously unpublished, resistance-conferring mutations of HIV Reverse Transcriptase (e.g. K102Y, T216M) and HIV Protease (e.g. Q18N, N88G) from our dataset. This led us to the next step of the study , the identification of novel mutations ( present in our dataset but not previously published ) which are found to confer cross resistance to antiretroviral treatments . Mutations were filtered using the following parameters: have a negative effect on the majority of drugs in a single class; occurrence in the dataset more than once; average Log FC for all compounds >0 . 4; standard deviation over this average <0 . 4 ... using literature we discarded any previously known mutations and kept those mutations that were novel . This provided us with a number of mutations that lead to an increase in fold change on average , again using literature we discarded any previously known mutations and kept those mutations that were novel .

fact: Proteochemometric models can accurately predict phenotypic resistance from genotypic data even for novel HIV mutants and mixtures.
source_span: We conclude that proteochemometric models are able to accurately predict the phenotypic resistance based on genotypic data even for novel mutants and mixtures. Given the wealth of training data present , the resulting bioactivity models can be used to predict the activity of clinical ARV drugs on mutants not present ( untested ) in the dataset ( corresponding to a patient with a new , previously unseen genotype that needs to be treated in the clinic ) . Hence, PCM is on the current dataset also able to extrapolate the Log FC values for individual pairs of drug and mutant not encountered in the training set with reliability comparable to assay reliability when the mutant in question is not present in the training set (External validation). To further find the limitations of this extrapolation we employed leave-one-sequence-out (LOSO) validation. LOSO validation is unique to proteochemometric approaches, since it enables the prediction of compound activities for entirely novel genotypes (or patients).
abstract_sentence: Proteochemometric models can accurately predict phenotypic resistance from genotypic data even for novel HIV mutants and mixtures.

fact: An applicability domain was added to the prediction to inform users about the reliability of predictions based on similarity to known sequences.
