source_span: This study reveals a novel role for ClfB during SSTIs . ClfB is crucial in determining the abscess structure and bacterial burden early in infection and this is dependent upon a specific interaction with the ligand loricrin which is expressed within the abscess tissue . Mice infected with LAC::lux ΔclfB formed significantly smaller abscess lesions on day 3–6 compared to mice infected with LAC::lux ( Fig 1A and 1B ) . The bioluminescence signal was also reduced in LAC::lux ΔclfB infected animals compared to LAC::lux infected mice ( Fig 1C and 1D ) . The reduction in bioluminescence signal was validated by quantifying the bacterial burden in the skin on day 3 ( Fig 1E ) and day 6 ( Fig 1F ) . Importantly, it can be seen that abscess formation is impaired in Lor-/- mice at 12 hours post infection with overall less well-structured and smaller abscesses being formed.
abstract_sentence: ClfB is crucial for abscess structure and bacterial burden early in skin infection through a specific interaction with loricrin expressed in abscess tissue.

fact: Targeting ClfB with a model vaccine that induces both humoral and cellular immune responses leads to protection during S. aureus skin infection.
source_span: Targeting ClfB using a model vaccine that induced both protective humoral and cellular responses , leads to protection during S . aureus skin infection . Immunization with ClfB in combination with CpG drove a significant increase in ClfB-specific IFNγ, IL-17 and IL-22 producing CD4+ T cells ... Vaccination with ClfB also induced significantly elevated ClfB-specific serum IgG titres in mice compared to the control group. We confirmed that these antibodies were functional by investigating their ability to inhibit L. lactis expressing ClfB to bind to immobilised loricrin. Mice vaccinated with ClfB in combination with CpG developed significantly smaller abscess lesions throughout the 6-day infection period compared to those vaccinated with adjuvant alone ... and the bacterial burden in the skin of ClfB vaccinated mice was decreased throughout the course of infection as measured by bioluminescence .
abstract_sentence: Vaccination targeting ClfB induces protective humoral and cellular immune responses and reduces severity of Staphylococcus aureus skin infection.

fact: ClfB is identified as an important antigen for future vaccines specifically targeting S. aureus skin and soft tissue infections.
source_span: This study therefore identifies ClfB as an important antigen for future SSTI vaccines . The development of an anti-S . aureus vaccine offers a potential solution to prevent infection regardless of antibiotic resistance; however , although significant efforts have been made , an effective anti-S . aureus vaccine remains elusive . Given the wide spectrum of pathologies caused by this bacterium it is unlikely that a universal anti-S . aureus vaccine will ever be realised [6] , and instead , a vaccine targeting specific clinical manifestations may need to be pursued .
abstract_sentence: ClfB is an important antigen for future vaccines targeting Staphylococcus aureus skin and soft tissue infections.

fact: Dengue virus (DENV) is the most prevalent arbovirus causing an estimated 100 million symptomatic dengue infections annually.
source_span: Dengue virus ( DENV ) is the most prevalent arbovirus leading to an estimated 100 million symptomatic dengue infections every year .
abstract_sentence: Dengue virus (DENV) is the most prevalent arbovirus causing an estimated 100 million symptomatic dengue infections annually.

fact: DENV infection can cause a range of clinical manifestations from mild dengue fever (DF) to life-threatening dengue hemorrhagic fever (DHF).
source_span: DENV can cause a spectrum of clinical manifestations , ranging from mild dengue fever ( DF ) to more life threatening forms such as dengue hemorrhagic fever ( DHF ) .
abstract_sentence: DENV infection can cause a range of clinical manifestations from mild dengue fever (DF) to life-threatening dengue hemorrhagic fever (DHF).

fact: The critical phase of dengue infection occurs 5–7 days after fever onset and is when symptoms of DHF typically become evident; the mechanisms triggering transition from DF to DHF are not well understood.
source_span: The clinical symptoms of DHF become evident typically at the critical phase of infection ( 5–7 days after onset of fever ) , yet the mechanisms that trigger transition from DF to DHF are not well understood .
abstract_sentence: The critical phase of dengue infection occurs 5–7 days after fever onset and is when symptoms of DHF typically become evident; however, the mechanisms triggering transition from DF to DHF are not well understood.

fact: Mass spectrometry-based metabolomic profiling was performed on sera from adult DF and DHF patients at critical and recovery phases.
source_span: We performed a mass spectrometry-based metabolomic profiling of sera from adult DF and DHF patients at the critical and recovery phases of infection . In the present study , metabolomics investigation was conducted on the same patient cohort at the critical phase ( day 5–7 post onset of fever ) and recovery phase ( day 21–28 post onset of fever ) to map the serum metabolome and identify metabolic pathways linked to dengue progression .
abstract_sentence: This study performed mass spectrometry-based metabolomic profiling of sera from adult DF and DHF patients at the critical and recovery phases of infection.

fact: 29 metabolites were differentially expressed between DF and DHF at the critical phase.
source_span: There were 29 differentially expressed metabolites identified between DF and DHF at the critical phase .
abstract_sentence: Twenty-nine metabolites were differentially expressed between DF and DHF patients at the critical phase.

fact: Differentially expressed metabolites include bile acids, purines, acylcarnitines, phospholipids, and amino acids.
source_span: These differentially expressed metabolites belonged to classes such as bile acid , acylcarnitine , phosphatidylcholine ( PC ) , lysophosphatidylcholine ( LysoPC ) , amino acid and derivative , dipeptide , purine and pyrimidine ( Table 1 ). The perturbed metabolic pathways in DHF in the critical phase included bile acid biosynthesis , fatty acid β-oxidation , purine and pyrimidine metabolism , phospholipid catabolism , tryptophan and phenylalanine metabolism .
abstract_sentence: Differentially expressed metabolites between DHF and DF at the critical phase include bile acids, purines, acylcarnitines, phospholipids, and amino acids, reflecting altered metabolic pathways.

fact: Bile acids were up to 5 fold higher in DHF than DF patients and correlated with higher AST and ALT levels, suggesting liver injury.
source_span: Bile acids were observed up to 5 fold higher levels among DHF compared to DF patients and were significantly correlated to the higher levels of aspartate transaminase ( AST ) and alanine transaminase ( ALT ) , suggestive of liver injury among DHF . Among them , the levels of the bile acids showed about 5 times higher in DHF patients than in DF patients ( Fig 2 ). Furthermore , these bile acids demonstrated positive correlations to AST and ALT levels , indicating they may be associated with liver dysfunction in DHF ( Fig 3 ). Put together , elevated bile acids among DHF patients and their positive correlations to AST and ALT levels indicated that these bile acids may play an important role in liver pathology in DHF patients .
abstract_sentence: Bile acids were up to fivefold higher in DHF patients compared to DF patients at the critical phase and correlated with elevated liver enzymes AST and ALT, indicating liver injury in DHF.

fact: Uric acid was 1.5 fold lower in DHF compared to DF patients, indicating decreased antioxidant defense.
source_span: Uric acid , the most abundant antioxidant in the blood , was observed to be 1 . 5 fold lower among DHF compared to DF patients . This could result in decreased capacity of endogenous antioxidant defense and elevated oxidative stress among DHF patients .
abstract_sentence: Uric acid, the most abundant antioxidant in blood, was 1.5 fold lower in DHF patients compared to DF patients, suggesting reduced antioxidant defense and increased oxidative stress in DHF.

fact: Eight metabolites including chenodeoxyglycocholic acid remained altered in DHF patients at recovery phase, indicating prolonged liver effects.
source_span: In the recovery phase , the levels of eight metabolites were still significantly higher or lower among DHF patients , including chenodeoxyglycocholic acid , one of the bile acids observed at the critical phase . This indicates potential prolonged adverse impact on the liver due to DENV infection in DHF patients . Among these differentially expressed metabolites , the level of the bile acid , chenodeoxyglycocholic acid , was still about 3 times higher in DHF patients than in DF patients , indicating prolonged effects of DENV infection on DHF patients ( Fig 4 ).
abstract_sentence: At the recovery phase, levels of eight metabolites, including the bile acid chenodeoxyglycocholic acid, remained significantly altered in DHF patients, indicating prolonged liver impact.

fact: Altered metabolic pathways linked to DHF were identified in critical and recovery phases, offering insights into disease mechanisms.
source_span: Our study identified altered metabolic pathways linked to DHF in the critical and recovery phases of dengue infection and provided insights into the different host and DENV interactions between DF and DHF . In summary , our study identified differentially expressed metabolites and the underlying metabolic pathways linked to DHF in both the critical and recovery phases of dengue infection .
abstract_sentence: The study identified altered metabolic pathways linked to DHF during critical and recovery phases, providing insights into host-virus interactions and DHF pathogenesis.

fact: Altered metabolic pathways identified in DHF might serve as therapeutic targets to alleviate the disease.
source_span: The results advance our understanding on the mechanisms of DHF pathogenesis , alluding to possible novel therapeutic targets to dengue management . These results provide insights into the mechanisms of DHF pathogenesis , and certain altered pathways might serve as therapeutic targets to alleviate DHF .
abstract_sentence: The findings suggest possible novel therapeutic targets for dengue management based on metabolic pathway alterations in DHF.

fact: Abundance of substrate receptor subunits of Cullin-RING ubiquitin ligases (CRLs) is tightly controlled to maintain the full repertoire of CRLs.
source_span: Abundance of substrate receptor subunits of Cullin-RING ubiquitin ligases ( CRLs ) is tightly controlled to maintain the full repertoire of CRLs .
abstract_sentence: Abundance of substrate receptor subunits of Cullin-RING ubiquitin ligases (CRLs) is tightly controlled to maintain the full repertoire of CRLs.

fact: Misregulation of substrate receptor components of CRLs, especially SCF ligases, has been linked to diseases including cancer.
source_span: Numerous diseases , including cancer , have been associated with misregulation of substrate receptor components , particularly for the largest class of CRLs , the SCF ligases .
abstract_sentence: Misregulation of substrate receptor components of CRLs, especially SCF ligases, has been associated with numerous diseases including cancer.

fact: F-box proteins are controlled by autocatalytic ubiquitylation by intact SCF complex followed by proteasome-mediated degradation.
source_span: One relevant mechanism that controls abundance of their substrate receptors , the F-box proteins , is autocatalytic ubiquitylation by intact SCF complex followed by proteasome-mediated degradation .
abstract_sentence: F-box proteins, the substrate receptors of SCF ligases, are regulated by autocatalytic ubiquitylation followed by proteasome-mediated degradation.

fact: A novel ubiquitylation and degradation pathway acts on Met30 dissociated from Skp1.
source_span: Here we describe an additional pathway for regulation of F-box proteins on the example of yeast Met30 . This ubiquitylation and degradation pathway acts on Met30 that is dissociated from Skp1 . We were interested in how cells cope with the generated excess of Met30 because the well-described autocatalytic F-box protein degradation pathway [10 , 11] cannot act on Met30 during these conditions . Interestingly , degradation of the F-box protein Met30 was maintained and even slightly induced in response to cadmium stress ( Fig 1A ) . A mutant form of Met30 lacking its entire F-box domain ( Met30ΔFbox ) was constitutively unstable even though cells did not experience cadmium stress ( Fig 1B ) . These results suggest a proteolytic pathway that recognizes unbound ‘Skp1-free’ Met30 to avoid accumulation of excess unbound Met30 , which could bind substrates and shield them from recognition by fully assembled SCFMet30 complexes .
abstract_sentence: An additional degradation pathway targets the yeast F-box protein Met30 when it is dissociated from Skp1.

fact: The pathway requires Cdc53/Cul1 but not Skp1.
source_span: Unexpectedly , this pathway required the cullin component Cdc53/Cul1 but was independent of the other central SCF component Skp1 . Unexpectedly , Cdc53 was indispensable for Met30ΔFbox degradation , because inactivation of the temperature sensitive cdc53-1 allele blocked degradation ( Fig 2B ) . Consistent with results using temperature sensitive alleles of skp1 , Met30ΔFbox degradation was unaffected when Skp1 function was blocked using the skp1-td strategy ( Fig 3C ) . The experiments with skp1 single and skp1 cdc53 double mutants strongly suggested that the ‘Skp1-free’ degradation pathway for Met30 was dependent on Cdc53 and independent of Skp1
abstract_sentence: This non-canonical degradation pathway requires the cullin component Cdc53/Cul1 but is independent of the SCF component Skp1.

fact: This pathway is important for chromosome stability and protection against heavy metal stress.
source_span: We demonstrated that this non-canonical degradation pathway is critical for chromosome stability and effective defense against heavy metal stress . Cells expressing Met30M178E/I179E were significantly more sensitive and exhibited a growth arrest in response to cadmium stress.
abstract_sentence: The non-canonical Met30 degradation pathway is critical for chromosome stability and defense against heavy metal stress in yeast.

fact: The pathway involves Cdc53, Rbx1, and Cdc34 but is independent of Skp1.
source_span: This degradation pathway targets Met30 that is detached from Skp1 and involves the SCF core components Cdc53 and Rbx1 , as well as the cognate SCF ubiquitin conjugating enzyme Cdc34 . Importantly , this ubiquitylation pathway does not require Skp1 ( Skp1-independent Cul1-dependent ubiquitylation ) and suggests a function of Cdc53/Cul1 that is independent from association with Skp1 . Surprisingly , degradation of Met30ΔFbox was dependent on the canonical SCF E2 , Cdc34 ( Fig 2B ) ... degradation was dependent on Cdc53 but not Skp1 . Met30ΔFbox degradation was greatly reduced in a strain expressing a 13Myc-tagged version of the RING finger component Rbx1 , which has previously been shown to be a hypomorph allele that results in reduced SCF function at high temperature ( Fig 2B ) . Not only was Met30 degradation active in the absence of Skp1 in vivo, but in addition a Cdc53 mutant incapable of binding to Skp1 could fully complement the Met30 degradation defect of cdc53 mutants. In addition, Cdc53/Rbx1 can directly bind Met30 in the absence of Skp1 in vitro and binding depends on the degron region adjacent to the F-box motif.
abstract_sentence: The non-canonical degradation pathway for unbound Met30 involves the SCF core components Cdc53, Rbx1, and the ubiquitin conjugating enzyme Cdc34 but does not require Skp1.
